scenario: A11 / CONTRACT.md Git HEAD: a SHA-256 object-format repository whose rev-parse HEAD is 64-hex (accepted by HeadSchema) must be observable and usable for handoff.submit and context.get currentGit
expected: observeCheckout accepts a 64-hex HEAD, handoff.submit completes the claimed task, and context.get reports that head instead of an observation error
observed: Originally required exactly 40 hex. Muse repair on fingerprint 9113834e uses GIT_HEAD_RE 40-or-64 in observeCheckout and observeCurrentGit. Independent rerun of the original reproduction now exits 0.
suggestedFix: In observeCheckout (line 56) and observeCurrentGit (line 92), accept the same 40- or 64-hex pattern as HeadSchema. Add a tests/storage case that git-inits with --object-format=sha256.
verificationExpectation: Original reproduction exits 0; new core test covers SHA-256 observation and completion.

scenario: A18: renderContext(snapshot, 4000) for a legal snapshot with 20 direct dependencies whose titles are at the 200-character write limit. Every dependency ID and status must remain; titles may be shortened; output must be <= 4000 characters
expected: Rendered length <= 4000 and every dependency.id and dependency.status still appear in full

suggestedFix: Reserve task ID/status/title and every dependency ID/status; shorten titles to fit before any hard slice. Add a 20-title 4000-char render test.
verificationExpectation: Original reproduction exits 0; new render test keeps every dependency ID at 4000.

scenario: A01: initialize from two processes concurrently; both must succeed, preserve data, keep one schema version. Independent G4 npm run check failed tests/storage/lifecycle.test.ts 'initializes from two processes concurrently without losing data'. Tight two-process openCore loop then failed 5 of 12 iterations with the same envelope.
expected: Two independent Node processes opening the same new home at once each complete openCore and their first mutation successfully. Failures are BUSY only when a lock cannot be acquired within 5000 ms, never an unmapped IO initialize error, and concurrent first startup does not lose a process.
observed: Originally 5/12 two-process first opens returned IO cannot initialize database; npm run check failed A01 concurrent init. Muse repair retries pragma/WAL/chmod/migrate on busy/locked errors within BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS and maps exhausted contention to CoreOpenError BUSY. Independent rerun of reports/grok/repro-a01-concurrent.mjs exits 0 (12/12). npm run check 169/169 including the new 6-round GROK-003 test.
suggestedFix: In openDatabase, treat busy/locked errors from pragma setup and migrate as retryable startup contention: bounded retry (within the existing 5000 ms busy timeout) of foreign_keys/busy_timeout/WAL/chmod/migrate until both concurrent openers succeed. Map exhausted contention to CoreOpenError BUSY, never 'cannot initialize database'. Add or keep the two-process A01 test and a tighter regression that fails if either child returns IO on first open. Do not skip the test or lengthen sleeps to hide the race. Owned files only (src/storage/db.ts and tests/storage/lifecycle.test.ts).
verificationExpectation: reports/grok/repro-a01-concurrent.mjs exits 0 over 12 iterations; npm run test:core includes the concurrent A01 test in green; Grok will rerun the original reproduction and the full gate before closing.

scenario: CONTRACT checkout of this project: handoff.submit with checkoutRoot of an unrelated repo (or independent clone with matching HEAD) must be rejected without completing the task or writing a handoff/receipt. Linked worktrees of the registered project must be accepted.
expected: CONFLICT, task remains running, no handoff row, no success receipt; same-project worktree completes
observed: On 0ef592a3 the foreign checkout completed the task. Muse repair compares discoverProject(checkout).gitCommonDir to the registered project inside the write transaction. Independent Codex reproduce.mjs now reports accepted=false taskStatus=CONFLICT. Tests in tests/storage/handoffs.test.ts cover foreign repo, matching-HEAD clone, and linked worktree.
suggestedFix: After receipt-first and outside-transaction Git collection, compare checkout git common dir to project.git_common_dir; CONFLICT with no writes on mismatch.
verificationExpectation: foreign-checkout scenario rejected; clone with same HEAD rejected; worktree accepted; npm run test:core green

scenario: A5/A6 lease equality: a renew/release/handoff dispatched before expiry that waits behind a SQLite write lock until after expiry must be STALE_CLAIM with no effects. A claim granted after a lock wait starts its 2h lease at acquisition time.
expected: Clock sampled after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, immediately before lease checks. Exact receipt replay still succeeds after expiry.
observed: On 0ef592a3 dispatch sampled nowMs before the lock wait; a renewal started before expiry and finished after it succeeded. Muse now passes the clock into transactMutation and samples it inside withWrite. Codex reproduce.mjs reports accepted=false result=STALE_CLAIM for renew-after-lock-wait.
suggestedFix: Sample now() after acquiring the write lock; keep observation timestamps separate; preserve receipt-first replay.
verificationExpectation: renew/release/handoff across expiry are STALE with unchanged row; post-wait claim lease starts at acquisition; exact renew replay still works

scenario: A22 / read-only Git: observeCheckout and observeCurrentGit must not change .git/index. A content-clean tree with only mtime touch must stay content-clean and leave index bytes identical.
expected: index bytes unchanged; dirty=false for mtime-only touch
observed: On 0ef592a3 git status refreshed the index. Muse prefixes every git subprocess with --no-optional-locks. Codex reproduce.mjs reports indexChanged=false reportedDirty=false.
suggestedFix: Pass git --no-optional-locks as an argument-array prefix; do not change user Git config.
verificationExpectation: index bytes identical after handoff+context+worktree observe; dirty false
